questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"In his masterpiece short story 'Toba Tek Singh', the celebrated Urdu writer Saadat Hasan Manto used the metaphor of a lunatic asylum to convey the absurdity of Partition: 'A couple of years after the Partition, the governments of Pakistan and India decided to exchange lunatic inmates in their asylums—Hindu and Sikh lunatics in Pakistan were to be handed over to India, and Muslim lunatics in India were to be transferred to Pakistan... One inmate, Bishan Singh, a Sikh landowner from the town of Toba Tek Singh, had been in the asylum for fifteen years. He constantly asked where Toba Tek Singh was located—was it in India or Pakistan? No one, not even the guards, could tell him clearly. When taken to the border at Wagah for exchange, he refused to cross over. In the morning, he collapsed. There, on a piece of land that had no name, lay Toba Tek Singh.'"

Where did Bishan Singh ultimately collapse and die at the Wagah border crossing?

options.text: At the railway platform in Amritsar

Detailed Solution:

questionText:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
 
 "The British element is
gone, but they have left the mischief behind"
 
It is no use saying that we ask for separate electorates, because it is good
for us. We have heard it long enough. We have heard it for years, and as a
result of this agitation, we are now a separate nation … Can you show me
one free country where there are separate electorates? If so, I shall be
prepared to accept it. But in this unfortunate country if this separate
electorate is going to be persisted in, even after the division of the country,
woe betide the country; it is not worth living in. Therefore, I say, it is not for
my good alone, it is for your own good that I say it, forget the past. One
day, we may be united … The British element is gone, but they have left the
mischief behind. We do not want to perpetuate that mischief. (Hear, hear).
When the British introduced this element they had not expected that they
will have to go so soon. They wanted it for their easy administration. That
is all right. But they have left the legacy behind. Are we to get out of it or
not?.
According to the speaker, what was the consequence of the policy of a
separate electorates?
